correctness.rationale: For each r in (0,1), F_r(alpha)=r-2r(1-r)alpha-r²(1-r)alpha²; the quartic sum of squares has derivative with coefficient signs (+,+,sign(m2),-) descending and exactly one positive zero by Descartes and endpoint signs. Under r_n=1-a/sqrt(n) and alpha=n^(1/4) beta, M_n/n converges locally uniformly to (1-a beta²)^2+D² beta⁴. A single t-eigenvalue and the O(n) trial bound keep minimizers beta bounded; the unique limit beta*=sqrt(a/(a²+D²)) gives the three ratios and actual sign-iterate error. 2aD<=a²+D² shows sharp 1/2 within stated family; norm comparison proves universal sqrt(n) order only. Independent separate two-level derivative bisection on n=4^4 through 256^4 confirmed beta→2 and spectral spike→1/2, not a proof of limits.
